royal-game-of-ur.evidence: J. Paul Getty Trust museum activity packet, PDF pages 13–15 only; the unchanged original contains other games. This is Getty’s playable seven-piece reconstruction adapted from Irving Finkel’s Games, not a surviving ancient rulebook or a claim that every modern variant agrees. Uses a six-sided die rerolled on 5/6, colored-square extra throws, exact exit, and doubled pieces that move together and are safe. That doubling rule differs from the current summary’s no-stacking variant. Board/path diagrams must be consulted in the original PDF.

ashtapada.evidence: Modern reconstruction published as a six-page A4 Games Company printable booklet; PDF pages 1–3 contain the introduction and all 27 numbered rules, while pages 4–6 are printable board/counters/casting sticks retained in the unchanged original. Not evidence of uniquely authentic ancient rules. Four sticks/cowries score 1–4, with all backs scoring 8; enter on 1, repeat throws until 2/3, use a player-specific spiral route, capture/re-enter, use safe marked squares/twins, exact entry to the keep and bear off on 1. The booklet has an inconsistent optional 1–5 spinner/strategy paragraph, and uses twins/keep terminology without a full glossary; those ambiguities are preserved rather than silently repaired. Use the casting-stick rules and original route diagram when consulting this reconstruction.
